newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says following JSDA rules on IPOs.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says following JSDA rules on IPOs.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it believed it was following Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) rules concerning initial public offerings (IPO).
"Concerning the allocation of shares at the time of initial public offerings, we understand that we are handling the subscriptions appropriately, based on JSDA rules," a Nomura spokesman said.

The spokesman however, declined comment on a newspaper report which said that prosecutors appeared to have questioned Nomura executives about transactions in shares of a major consumer loan firm before the firm's IPO.

The report, in the financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun, said prosecutors were looking into whether there were dubious transfers of the loan firm's shares to politicians and government officials prior to the IPO.
"We have not confirmed (the report) so we have no comment," the Nomura spokesman said.

A spokesman for Takefuji Corp told Reuters separately that the newspaper report probably referred to Takefuji, which is Japan's biggest consumer finance company and which debuted on the over-the-counter market in August 1996.
The Takefuji spokesman added that Takefuji had not been questioned by prosecutors and that the company had done nothing wrong.

Takefuji and the Finance Ministry were, however, embarrassed by news last October that a former Finance Ministry official, who was a part-time auditor for the firm, was offered its shares prior to the public offering.
Neither the firm nor the ex-official was accused of breaking any laws in the share deal and Takefuji said at the time it saw nothing amiss in the transaction.
